messages.subject: c++ program as targetRunner on linux
parts:
Hello,

I am a student and I am starting to use irace. I wrote a c++ program as the targetRunner. I am running irace on Linux. I believe I have delt with the command line arguments accurately. When I run the --check command as specified in the user guide it says that the check is unsuccessful and that targetRunner returns null. So I tried calling one line that irace calls as specified in the user guide but I get a bunch of errors like "int: command not found", "int: no such file or directory", "syntax error near unexpected token '(' " etc.

So to make it more clear when I run one line that irace calls I run:
/home/joca/Desktop/iraceOpet/simulirano_kaljenje.cpp    testConfig1    1    1234567    /home/joca/Desktop/iraceOpet/Instances/AP102.tsp    --maxi    20993

and I get errors like:
/home/joca/Desktop/iraceOpet/simulirano_kaljenje.cpp:    line 14: int: command not found
...

(actually valgrind and check also detect the same errors)
but when I run my code like    ./a.out    simulirano_kaljenje.cpp    testConfig1    1    1234567   /home/joca/Desktop/iraceOpet/Instances/AP102.tsp    --maxi    20993
this works as it should. Keeping in mind that I did change the indexes of argv (do to ./a.out)

If you are familiar with the problem I would appreciate the help. :)

On Wednesday, 15 July 2020 21:29:29 UTC+2, Jovana Radjenovic wrote:

Hello,

I am a student and I am starting to use irace. I wrote a c++ program as the targetRunner. I am running irace on Linux. I believe I have delt with the command line arguments accurately. When I run the --check command as specified in the user guide it says that the check is unsuccessful and that targetRunner returns null. So I tried calling one line that irace calls as specified in the user guide but I get a bunch of errors like "int: command not found", "int: no such file or directory", "syntax error near unexpected token '(' " etc.

So to make it more clear when I run one line that irace calls I run:
/home/joca/Desktop/iraceOpet/simulirano_kaljenje.cpp    testConfig1    1    1234567    /home/joca/Desktop/iraceOpet/Instances/AP102.tsp    --maxi    20993

and I get errors like:
/home/joca/Desktop/iraceOpet/simulirano_kaljenje.cpp:    line 14: int: command not found
...

Hi Jovana,

If simulirano_kaljenje.cpp is a C++ file, you first need to compile it to get an executable file (perhaps a.out is the file you compiled?).
(actually valgrind and check also detect the same errors)
It is a good idea to check with valgrind. If valgrind complains, then it is not a problem in irace. The problem is somewhere else.

but when I run my code like    ./a.out    simulirano_kaljenje.cpp    testConfig1    1    1234567   /home/joca/Desktop/iraceOpet/Instances/AP102.tsp    --maxi    20993
this works as it should. Keeping in mind that I did change the indexes of argv (do to ./a.out)

If a.out is compiled from simulirano_kaljenje.cpp then you don't need  to use simulirano_kaljenje.cpp when executing a.out.
 
This is not a problem with irace but I hope the above helps.

Best,

Manuel.
